title: Space Tech Briefing — September 13, 2026
summary:
Good morning, space enthusiasts, and welcome to your daily dose of the cosmos! It's Saturday, September 13, 2026, and we've got some truly stellar news for you today, including an incredible opportunity to leave your mark on space history!

First up, get ready to unleash your creativity! The French space agency, CNES, has just announced an amazing competition. They're inviting YOU to help name the upcoming missions of two incredible French astronauts: Thomas Pesquet and Arnaud Prost! Both are set to embark on distinct space missions in 2027. That's right, two different missions, and the chance to name both of them is now open to the public. Imagine having your chosen name soaring among the stars! It's a fantastic way to connect directly with the future of human spaceflight. Stay tuned to CNES channels for all the details on how to submit your brilliant ideas.

And as we wait for today's new launches and future mission names, let's look back at a major recent development that continues to expand our understanding of the universe. We're talking about the incredible Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite, or TESS! This exoplanet hunter, launched back in 2018, has been diligently scanning the heavens for worlds beyond our solar system. NASA recently unveiled the most comprehensive sky map ever produced by TESS. This colossal mosaic, compiled from observations taken between April 2018 and September 2025, stitches together an astonishing 96 sectors of the sky. It reveals nearly 6,000 vibrant objects, each representing a confirmed or candidate exoplanet! TESS truly continues to redefine our cosmic neighborhood, one distant world at a time.

What an exciting time to be looking up! From naming future missions to marveling at new exoplanet discoveries, the universe is constantly calling. That's all for your morning briefing. Have a fantastic day, and keep looking to the stars!
